sentences.english_text: The computer that Drippy had chosen controlled all the other computers in the building.
Now, as we already know, moisture affects the computers so that they cannot work properly.
And when Drippy climbed inside the master computer, it went crazy.
Needles began to move and lights began to flash and alarm bells began to ring.
What's happening?
The man in uniform cried.
No one knew.
Because the master computer controlled all the other computers, all of them began to go wild.
I think we're under attack.
A general cried.
All the majors and colonels and generals raced over to study their machines.
I think Russian planes are coming.
No, it's submarines.
It's missiles.
The mixed up computers showed that the United States was being attacked from the north and the south and the east and the west.
It showed that the attack was coming from the air, the ground and the sea.
You have never seen such panic.
A general got on the hotline and telephoned the president.
Mr. President, I think we're under attack.
By whom?
We're not sure, Mr. President.
The computers are acting very strangely.
Should we launch our missiles?
The president thought for a moment.
Well, call a red alert and get the missiles ready.
And don't launch them until you have more information.
I'll be right over.
